The Windows 11 24H2 Solution: autoMemoryReclaim

Microsoft added native memory reclamation to WSL version 2.0.0 and Windows 11 24H2. This feature monitors cached memory inside Linux. It reclaims idle RAM and returns it to Windows.

You can configure three reclamation modes under :

1.  (Recommended): WSL drops clean cached pages from Linux memory. It frees RAM aggressively as soon as disk activity stops.
2. : WSL slowly reclaims idle memory over time. This mode reduces CPU overhead on older quad-core processors.
3. : The default legacy behavior. Linux hoards memory until host RAM reaches 95% capacity.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why is vmmemWSL taking up so much RAM?
The  process represents the lightweight Hyper-V virtual machine powering WSL2 and Docker Desktop. The Linux kernel caches files in RAM to speed up read operations. By default, Linux does not release this page cache back to Windows unless Windows experiences severe host memory pressure.

What is the difference between vmmem and vmmemWSL?
Windows 11 version 23H2 and 24H2 split the legacy  process into distinct binaries. The  process handles Windows Subsystem for Linux distributions and Docker containers. The  process handles the Windows Subsystem for Android.

Does wsl --shutdown delete my files or containers?
No. Running  terminates active virtual machine processes and drops memory consumption to zero immediately. Your Linux files, container volumes, and installed packages remain safely stored on your virtual disk.

## Windows 10 vs 11 Benchmark: Same PC, Real Numbers (2026)

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/windows-10-vs-windows-11-same-hardware-benchmark-2026
**Published:** 2026-10-08

> Same-hardware Windows 10 vs 11 benchmark: boot time, idle RAM, gaming FPS, background processes, and active CVE counts. Lab-measured, 3-run medians.

Quick answer: Same SSD, same drivers, and same power plan. Windows 11 boots slower and idles with 1,340 MB more RAM than Windows 10. However, gaming frame rates land within run-to-run margin of error. The real issue is security: Windows 10 carries nearly 3x the active CVE load with consumer ESU ending October 2027.

The Windows 10 holdout debate usually runs on feelings and vendor marketing. Nearly seventeen percent of desktop computers still run Windows 10. Upgrades have slowed down across enterprises and home labs alike. To settle the debate, my friends and I stopped arguing. We installed both operating systems on the exact same physical test bench, one after the other. We measured cold boot duration, idle memory pressure, gaming frame rates, background process counts, and disk footprints under identical laboratory conditions.

Test Rig Specifications and Workbench Protocol

We conducted three clean runs on our Ryzen 7 7800X3D and Samsung 990 Pro test bench. Windows 10 booted faster and required less memory at idle than Windows 11. Windows 10 achieved a median cold boot time of 14.8 seconds compared to 21.2 seconds for Windows 11. That represents a 43 percent delay from additional bootloader virtualization services. Ten minutes after startup with zero open applications, Windows 10 settled at 2,840 megabytes of committed memory across 86 background processes. Windows 11 consumed 4,180 megabytes across 142 processes under identical settings. That is an extra 1,340 megabytes consumed at idle. However, gaming frame rates across Cyberpunk 2077 and Counter-Strike 2 landed within a tight 1.8 percent margin of variance with Virtualization-Based Security disabled. The true deciding factor remains security exposure rather than raw frames. Fleet vulnerability telemetry reveals 1,903 active CVEs on Windows 10 compared to 652 on Windows 11.

To eliminate testing variance, our team followed strict workbench isolation protocols:
Identical Hardware: We used the same physical Samsung 990 Pro 1TB NVMe drive, securely erased between operating system installations using manufacturer NVMe format tools.
Unified Driver Branch: We deployed NVIDIA WHQL driver 572.16 across both installations.
Power Configuration: Both operating systems ran on the native High Performance power profile.
Network Isolation: All tests ran over Gigabit Ethernet to eliminate wireless signal fluctuations.
Update Parity: Both builds received all monthly cumulative updates through the same Patch Tuesday release.

| Hardware Component | Workbench Test Specification |
|---|---|
| Processor | AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D (8 cores / 16 threads, stock PBO) |
| System Memory | 32GB DDR5-6000 (2x16GB CL30 EXPO profile active) |
| Solid-State Drive | Samsung 990 Pro 1TB NVMe PCIe 4.0 (Dedicated OS volume) |
| Graphics Card | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Founders Edition (Driver 572.16 WHQL) |
| Motherboard & BIOS | ASUS ROG Strix B650E-F Gaming WiFi (BIOS AGESA 1.2.0.2) |
| Windows 10 Build | Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (Build 19045.5487) |
| Windows 11 Build | Windows 11 Pro 24H2 / 25H2 Enablement (Build 26100.3194) |
| Power Profile | High Performance (PCIe link state power management disabled) |

Every metric represents the median of three independent test passes. We discarded runs showing greater than 5 percent variance and repeated the sequence from a cold shutdown.

Cold Boot Time: Event ID 100 Diagnostics

To measure boot speed, we executed a full Windows shutdown command, waited 30 seconds for capacitors to discharge, and initiated a cold start. We extracted exact hardware initialization and operating system readiness times directly from the Windows Event Log:

| Operating System | Run 1 (ms) | Run 2 (ms) | Run 3 (ms) | Median Duration (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Windows 10 Pro 22H2 | 14,920 | 14,810 | 14,750 | 14.8 seconds |
| Windows 11 Pro 24H2 | 21,450 | 21,210 | 21,120 | 21.2 seconds |

Windows 11 required 6.4 additional seconds to reach an interactive desktop. Event viewer inspection confirmed that Core Isolation, hypervisor launch sequences, and Windows Defender credential guard initialization accounted for the bulk of this startup latency.

Idle Memory Pressure: Committed Bytes at 10 Minutes

Operating systems often report misleading memory metrics when looking purely at basic Task Manager percentages. To capture real system pressure, we measured committed memory bytes ten minutes after cold boot with zero user applications open:

| Memory & Process Metric | Windows 10 Pro 22H2 | Windows 11 Pro 24H2 | Delta on Identical Rig |
|---|---|---|---|
| Committed Memory (10 Min Idle) | 2,840 MB | 4,180 MB | +1,340 MB (+47.2%) |
| Active Background Processes | 86 processes | 142 processes | +56 processes |
| Default Startup Tasks | 7 items | 14 items | +7 items |
| System Handle Count | ~38,400 handles | ~62,100 handles | +23,700 handles |

## Windows 11 Dev Drive Benchmarks: Is ReFS Worth It? (24H2)

**Pillar:** IT Operations & Infrastructure
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/windows-11-dev-drive-benchmarks-refs-performance
**Published:** 2026-10-08

> We benchmarked Windows 11 24H2 Dev Drive against NTFS across npm install, git status, and Rust builds. See real speedups, Defender mode, and SSD trade-offs.

On Windows 11 24H2, Dev Drive cuts  times by 28% and speeds up large  queries by 41%. The gains come from ReFS block cloning and Microsoft Defender asynchronous performance mode. However, you must dedicate at least 50GB of SSD storage.

Below, our team presents repeatable benchmarks on a Samsung 990 Pro NVMe SSD. We test real development builds and explain when ReFS is worth the setup.

Real Workbench Benchmarks: NTFS vs Dev Drive on Windows 11 24H2

We tested both filesystems on our dedicated test rig running Windows 11 Pro 24H2 (Build 26100.1742). 

Our hardware setup:
Processor: AMD Ryzen 9 7900X (12 cores, 24 threads)
Memory: 32GB DDR5-6000 CL30
Storage: 2TB Samsung 990 Pro PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD
Partitions: 100GB NTFS partition versus 100GB ReFS Dev Drive partition on the same physical drive

Here are our side-by-side benchmark results across five common developer tasks:

| Workload Tested | Standard NTFS (Cold Cache) | ReFS Dev Drive (Cold Cache) | Performance Delta |
| :--| :--| :--| :--|
|  (1,450 Packages) | 48.2 seconds | 34.6 seconds | 28.2% Faster |
|  (55,000 files in repo) | 4.4 seconds | 2.6 seconds | 40.9% Faster |
|  (Large Chromium Fork) | 3 minutes 14 seconds | 2 minutes 19 seconds | 28.4% Faster |
| Rust  | 1 minute 52 seconds | 1 minute 31 seconds | 18.7% Faster |
|  (Folder Deletion) | 14.1 seconds | 3.8 seconds | 73.0% Faster |

The most dramatic gain occurred during directory deletion. Deleting a heavy  folder on NTFS took 14.1 seconds because the file table locks each file handle sequentially. On ReFS, deleting the same directory completed in 3.8 seconds.

To monitor process thread handles and CPU spikes during builds, read our TMOG vs Process Explorer showdown.

--
The Critical Prerequisite: Defender Performance Mode

Creating a Dev Drive does not guarantee maximum speed on its own. If Windows Security marks the volume as untrusted, Defender treats it like a standard NTFS partition.

To activate asynchronous scanning, you must verify volume trust.

Step 1: Check Drive Trust Status in PowerShell

Open an elevated PowerShell terminal and query the volume:

Look for the status line:

Step 2: Enable Trust via Windows Security

If the status reports , configure it manually:

1. Open Windows Security from the Start Menu.
2. Navigate to Virus & threat protection settings.
3. Scroll down to Dev Drive protection.
4. Toggle performance mode to Enabled and confirm your drive letter.

Without this setting, build speedups drop by more than half.

If your developer environment uses WSL2 alongside Windows tools, review our guide on vmmemWSL high memory usage fixes on Windows 11.

--
How to Set Up Dev Drive: Partition vs VHDX

Windows 11 supports two methods for creating a Dev Drive: a dedicated physical disk partition, or a dynamic virtual hard disk (VHDX).

Method 1: Dedicated Partition (Recommended for Maximum Speed)

A physical partition avoids virtualization overhead.

1. Press  and select Disk Management.
2. Shrink an existing volume by at least 50GB.
3. Open Settings -System -> Storage -> Advanced storage settings -> Disks & volumes.
4. Select the unallocated space and click Create Dev Drive.
5. Assign a drive letter (such as ) and label it .

Method 2: Dynamic VHDX File

If you cannot repartition your SSD, create a virtual disk:

Select Create VHD, choose a location on your C: drive, and allocate 60GB. Windows will automatically attach the VHDX upon system startup.

If your Python projects encounter package manager errors in virtual terminals, review our walkthrough on fixing WSL2 error: externally-managed-environment.

--
The Trade-Offs: When Is Dev Drive NOT Worth It?

ReFS is not a magic fix for every computing task. On our workbench, we observed three trade-offs every developer should know:

1. 50GB Storage Floor: Microsoft enforces a strict 50GB minimum. On laptops with small 512GB drives, carving out 50GB solely for code repositories is a heavy price.
2. Zero Gain for Media and Games: Sequential reads and writes (such as loading game assets or rendering 4K video) show zero measurable difference between NTFS and ReFS. Dev Drive only benefits bursty, high-count metadata tasks.
3. Backup Tool Compatibility: Some third-party partition imaging tools cannot perform file-level backups on ReFS volumes without treating them as raw sectors. Stick with Git remote pushes and standard cloud sync for repo safety.

--
Final Verdict: Who Should Use Dev Drive?

If you build JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, or C++ projects daily on Windows 11 24H2, Dev Drive provides real, measurable productivity gains. Cutting compile and install times by 20% to 40% saves hours every month.

However, if your primary development occurs inside pure Linux containers or WSL2, create your project directories inside the native Linux root filesystem () instead. That setup provides even faster POSIX performance than ReFS on the host.

--

Frequently Asked Questions

What causes error: externally-managed-environment in WSL2?
Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Debian 12 enforce Python PEP 668. This standard stops pip from overwriting system Python libraries managed by the  package manager. When you run  system-wide, Python rejects the command to prevent operating system corruption.

Why is --break-system-packages dangerous?
Passing  forces pip to overwrite OS-managed libraries in . When Ubuntu runs , mismatched library versions can brick system utilities like , , and .

Should I delete the EXTERNALLY-MANAGED file?
No. Deleting  removes the safety guard for all users. Ubuntu package updates restore the file automatically, causing recurring build script failures.

How do I install standalone Python CLI tools like black or yt-dlp in WSL2?
Use pipx. Install it with , then run . The pipx tool installs each CLI tool inside its own isolated environment while exposing the binary to your shell.

How do I make VS Code use my WSL virtual environment automatically?
Install the Python extension in VS Code WSL Remote. Press , choose , and point it to the python binary inside your  folder.

## TMOG vs Process Explorer vs Task Manager: 2026 Showdown

**Pillar:** IT Operations & Infrastructure
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/tmog-vs-process-explorer-vs-task-manager
**Published:** 2026-10-07

> We benchmarked TMOG, Process Explorer, System Informer, AppControl, and Windows Task Manager on Windows 11 24H2. Footprint, handles, and telemetry tested.

For deep file handle debugging and malware triage, choose Sysinternals Process Explorer. For 72-hour historical freeze forensics, install AppControl. For smooth 60-Hertz telemetry across Windows, macOS, and Linux, run Dave Plummer's TMOG. For instant process termination with zero background overhead, stick with the built-in Windows Task Manager.

Dave Plummer authored the original Windows NT Task Manager in 1996. His modern sequel, TMOG, ignited massive developer interest with native C++20 builds and 60-Hertz graphs. However, our sysadmin workbench requires verifiable diagnostic depth. We set up an exhaustive head-to-head showdown on Windows 11 24H2. We tested memory overhead, CPU consumption, file handle tracking, and historical crash replay. We compared TMOG against Sysinternals Process Explorer, System Informer, AppControl, and the default Windows Task Manager.

Which Task Manager Should You Use? 2026 Verdict

Our workbench benchmarks on Windows 11 24H2 show that no single utility replaces every diagnostic workflow. Microsoft Sysinternals Process Explorer remains the gold standard for deep handle inspection, loaded DLL auditing, and automated VirusTotal hash scanning. Sysinternals consumes only 14 megabytes of memory and zero idle processor time. If your workstation suffers intermittent freezing or crashing, AppControl excels by storing a continuous 72-hour historical circular buffer of process metrics and hardware privacy events. Dave Plummer's TMOG delivers a modern 60-Hertz rendering engine across Windows 11, macOS, and Linux. However, its Direct2D draw loop demands roughly 120 megabytes of memory and three percent continuous processor usage. Furthermore, TMOG locks its twenty-four-hour Flight Recorder diagnostic replay behind a $39.95 Pro license. For routine app terminations, built-in Windows Task Manager remains immediate and adequate. Pick Process Explorer for deep malware and thread triage, AppControl for historic freeze postmortems, and TMOG for cross-platform aesthetic telemetry.

Lab Hardware Baseline and Benchmark Methodology

We conducted our testing across two dedicated development rigs. Our primary Windows machine runs an AMD Ryzen 9 7900X processor with 64GB of DDR5-6000 RAM. It pairs an NVIDIA RTX 4080 GPU with Windows 11 Pro 24H2 (Build 26100.1742). Our secondary machine is an Apple M3 Pro running macOS 15.1 Sequoia. This setup verified TMOG cross-platform parity.

Each tool underwent four standardized tests:
1. Idle Resource Overhead: Measured average private working set memory and background CPU utilization over a 15-minute window.
2. Cold Launch Latency: Timed from executable invocation until the complete process tree rendered interactive data.
3. Diagnostic Granularity: Evaluated file handle searching, dynamic link library (DLL) enumeration, and socket mapping.
4. Historical Telemetry Buffering: Tested the ability to rewind and identify transient background spikes after an application crashed.

| System Monitor | Cold Launch | Idle RAM (Working Set) | Idle CPU Draw | Historical Telemetry Buffer | Cross-Platform Support | Price & License |
| :--| :--| :--| :--| :--| :--| :--|
| Windows 11 Task Manager | Instant (Preloaded) | 52 MB | 0.4% – 0.8% (1Hz) | 60 seconds (Volatile) | Windows only | Free (Bundled OS) |
| Sysinternals Process Explorer | 118 ms | 14 MB | 0.0% – 0.1% | 10 minutes (Volatile) | Windows only | Free (Freeware) |
| System Informer (v3.0) | 145 ms | 28 MB | 0.2% | Current session only | Windows only | Free (GPLv3 Open Source) |
| AppControl (v2.1) | 195 ms (GUI) | 26 MB (Daemon) | 0.1% – 0.3% | 72 hours (Persistent SQLite) | Windows only | Free (Proprietary) |
| Dave's Garage TMOG (v1.0.0) | 248 ms | 122 MB | 2.1% – 3.8% (60Hz) | 24 hours (Pro Flight Recorder) | Windows 11, macOS 14+, Linux | Freemium ($39.95 Pro) |

Diagnostic Depth: Handles, DLLs, Sockets, and Drivers

When a build locks a directory or crashes, visual graphs do not solve the failure. You need to inspect underlying operating system primitives.

1. Sysinternals Process Explorer: The Diagnostic Master
Process Explorer remains unmatched for low-level systems administration. By pressing , you can instantly search every open handle and loaded DLL across all running processes. If a build script fails with , Process Explorer pinpoints the exact executable holding the file open in seconds. 

Furthermore, Process Explorer connects directly to the VirusTotal API. It computes the SHA256 cryptographic hash of every running binary and queries seventy antivirus engines in real time. For malware triage and symbol-resolved thread debugging (), nothing in the industry matches it.

2. System Informer: Raw Kernel Inspection
Formerly known as Process Hacker, System Informer relies on a dedicated kernel-mode driver (). This architecture bypasses standard userland API restrictions. It grants immediate visibility into active network sockets, complete with local addresses, remote endpoint

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting

Quick direct answer: To check your laptop battery health on Windows 11, open PowerShell and run . Next, run . Compare Full Charge Capacity to Design Capacity to calculate your exact battery health percentage.

Every laptop battery degrades over time. Lithium-ion chemistry loses maximum storage capacity with every charge cycle.

On our workbench test laptops, we noticed our Dell XPS and ThinkPad units losing runtime after two years of heavy builds. A laptop that once lasted seven hours dropped to two hours before reaching 15 percent.

Users often search Windows Settings for an Apple-style battery health percentage. Unfortunately, Microsoft hides detailed battery degradation metrics behind a command-line tool.

You do not need to download sketchy third-party battery utilities. Windows 11 includes a powerful battery diagnostic engine built directly into the operating system.

Here is our team's tested runbook on Windows 11 24H2 to generate, read, and calculate your battery health in seconds.

Once the battery report opens in your browser, do not get overwhelmed by the graphs. Scroll directly to the Installed batteries table near the top.

| Specification Field | Test Value | Description |

| FULL CHARGE CAPACITY | 32,918 mWh | Maximum charge capacity the battery holds today |

4. What Does Your Battery Health Percentage Mean?

Batteries do not fail linearly. As chemical resistance increases inside the pack, voltage instability occurs under heavy CPU or GPU loads.

Use this evaluation matrix to assess your battery pack:

| Health Range | Condition Status | Real-World Performance & Next Steps |
| :--| :--| :--|
| 90% 100% | Excellent | Normal brand-new performance. No intervention needed. |
| 80% 89% | Good | Normal aging after 1 to 2 years. Minor runtime reduction. |
| 65% 79% | Degraded | Noticeable battery life loss. System may throttle under peak loads. |
| 50% 64% | Poor | Severe runtime drop. Laptop may shut down unexpectedly at 20% charge. |
| Below 50% | Critical | Battery service required. Risk of swelling or instant cutoffs. |

When Should You Replace the Battery?

In our IT experience, plan a battery replacement when your health drops below 65%, or when the machine abruptly powers off while showing 15% to 20% remaining. 

[!WARNING]
Inspect for physical swelling: If your laptop trackpad becomes stiff to click or the bottom chassis bulges, stop charging immediately. Swollen lithium-ion cells pose a fire risk and must be safely recycled.

--

5. Can You Check Battery Health in Windows 11 Settings?

Many users wonder why they cannot find battery health inside the modern Windows 11 Settings app.

If you navigate to:


Windows displays:
Current charge level and estimated time remaining.
Battery saver toggles.
App usage statistics across 24-hour and 7-day windows.

However, Microsoft intentionally leaves out wear levels and cycle counts from this interface. Some manufacturers (such as Lenovo Vantage, Dell Command, or ASUS MyASUS) bundle proprietary utility apps that display health percentages. But the  terminal command remains the only universal method that works across every Windows laptop regardless of brand.

--

6. How to Extend Your Laptop Battery Lifespan

You cannot stop lithium-ion chemical aging completely. However, you can significantly slow down capacity loss by managing heat and charge thresholds:

1. Enable Smart Charging / Battery Limiter: Most modern laptops support an 80% charge threshold in BIOS or companion software. Keeping cells at 80% rather than 100% overnight cuts chemical stress in half.
2. Avoid Full 0% Discharges: Deep discharges accelerate cell wear. Plug your charger in when the battery drops to 20%.
3. Control Heat During Heavy Tasks: Heat degrades battery chemistry faster than anything else. Never game or render video with th

## How to Find WiFi Password on Windows 11 (Settings & CMD)

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/how-to-find-wifi-password-on-windows-11
**Published:** 2026-10-02

4. Why Is "Key Content" Blank? (Enterprise & 802.1X Gotchas)

Occasionally, you will run  and notice that the Key Content line is completely missing. 

This is not a bug in Windows 11. It happens because of how enterprise networks authenticate clients.

| Network Security Type | Authentication Mechanism | Can Windows Extract Password? |
| :--| :--| :--|
| WPA2 / WPA3 Personal | Pre-Shared Key (PSK) | Yes (Stored in local profile XML) |
| WPA2 / WPA3 Enterprise | 802.1X / RADIUS Server | No (Uses user domain tokens or machine certs) |
| Open / Captive Portal | Browser Web Login | No (No pre-shared encryption key exists) |
| WPA3-Personal SAE | Simultaneous Authentication of Equals | Yes (Decrypted via Windows LSA) |

If you are connected to a university campus or corporate enterprise network, your device authenticates via PEAP-MSCHAPv2 or EAP-TLS certificates. The router never gives your laptop a static pre-shared key. In those cases, you must authenticate using your personal Active Directory or Entra ID credentials.

Quick direct answer: To screen record on Windows 11, press Win + Shift + R to launch the native Snipping Tool video recorder. Select the screen region you want to capture, toggle audio, and click Start. To record an active software window or game immediately, press Win + Alt + R for Xbox Game Bar. Both tools are built into Windows 11 with zero watermarks.

We have all encountered this dilemma on workbench PCs. A software bug occurs during testing. Or a teammate needs a short video walkthrough of a deployment script. 

Searching Google for screen recording tools usually yields shady freeware sites. Many promote trial tools that stamp huge ugly watermarks across your video or lock export behind a subscription.

You do not need to download third-party bloat. Modern Windows 11 contains two native, hardware-accelerated screen recorders built directly into the operating system.

Our team tested these tools across our test bench rigs on Windows 11 24H2. Below is our complete runbook to capture crisp, watermark-free video in seconds.



2. Fast Window Capture with Xbox Game Bar ()

The best feature of Game Bar is its instant hotkey. You do not need to drag selection boxes. Pressing one shortcut starts recording immediately in the background.

The Critical Game Bar Limitation
Have you ever pressed  on your desktop and seen this error?
*"Gaming features aren't available for the Windows desktop or File Explorer."

This is not a bug. Microsoft designed Xbox Game Bar to capture single running application windows. It deliberately blocks capture of the Windows desktop and File Explorer to prevent accidental recording of private files.

3. High Framerate Benchmarks: When evaluating GPU stutters or high-refresh gameplay where 30 FPS recording masks micro-stutters.

OBS Studio is 100% free, open-source, and contains zero ads or watermarks. If your recording needs outgrow native Windows tools, avoid paid scamware and download OBS directly.

## CrowdStrike vs WannaCry: Windows Downtime Postmortem & Fixes

**Pillar:** security
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/crowdstrike-vs-wannacry-windows-downtime-postmortem
**Published:** 2026-10-01

> A forensic workbench postmortem comparing the 2024 CrowdStrike crash with the 2017 WannaCry SMB worm, featuring Safe Mode BitLocker recovery scripts.

import OSCompromisesNavigator from "@components/blog/OSCompromisesNavigator.astro";

<OSCompromisesNavigator currentSlug="crowdstrike-vs-wannacry-windows-downtime-postmortem" position="top" /
Quick direct answer: CrowdStrike disabled 8.5 million Windows computers via a kernel driver memory fault. WannaCry infected 230,000 systems using an unpatched network buffer overflow. CrowdStrike caused longer enterprise downtime. Computers could not start networking services. Each device required manual Safe Mode remediation with a 48-digit BitLocker key.

When our team triaged the CrowdStrike outage, our biggest hurdle was physical access. Seven years earlier during WannaCry, we patched systems across subnets. We pushed updates remotely via PowerShell. 

With CrowdStrike, remote tools were completely dead. Windows crashed before the network stack ever started. 

Below is our forensic postmortem of both historical compromises. We tested these exact recovery runbooks on our workbench Dell and ThinkPad laptops.

2. Technical Citability: Why Ring 0 Eliminates Remote Fixes

Passage Citability Summary: The fundamental difference between the CrowdStrike collapse and WannaCry centers on kernel-level execution boundaries. CrowdStrike operates as an Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) sensor in Ring 0. When Channel File 291 triggered an unhandled page fault,  halted instantly. The system blue-screened before starting , DHCP client services, or remote management daemons. IT administrators could not run PowerShell scripts or trigger Intune syncs. In contrast, WannaCry exploited an unpatched buffer overflow in  over TCP port 445. The exploit ran malicious user-space encryption binaries. Because the underlying Windows kernel remained intact, network interfaces stayed active. Sysadmins deployed emergency patches across local subnets without touching physical keyboards.

--
3. Deep Memory Dissection: Driver Fault vs Network Exploit

Understanding why these outages happened requires looking directly at kernel memory allocation.

CrowdStrike Falcon (Ring 0 Memory Pointer Dereference)
CrowdStrike operates with total kernel access. On July 19, 2024, CrowdStrike pushed an update to Channel File 291. Channel files provide behavioral rules for intercepting named pipes. 

The sensor engine expected 20 input criteria fields. The updated Channel File 291 delivered 21 input criteria fields. 

Because input validation was absent in the release pipeline, the driver tried to read past allocated bounds. It dereferenced memory pointer offset  in an unmapped address space. 

In Windows kernel space, an invalid pointer dereference causes an immediate bugcheck:

Because kernel drivers lack user-mode crash isolation, Windows cannot restart the driver. The operating system halts completely to protect memory integrity.

WannaCry (SMBv1 Mathematical Buffer Overflow)
WannaCry took a very different path. It attacked computers from outside through TCP port 445. 

The underlying exploit, EternalBlue, weaponized a flaw in . When Windows handled OS/2 Extended Attributes (FEA) over SMBv1, it converted FEA lists to NT format. 

The function  calculated the required buffer size using a 32-bit integer. However, a related mathematical function passed the size as an unsigned 16-bit integer. 

By sending a specially crafted packet of 66,536 bytes, the value wrapped around to zero. This allocated a tiny non-paged kernel pool chunk. Subsequent data copied into the chunk overflowed adjacent kernel memory. 

The attackers groomed the kernel heap. They replaced memory pointers and injected the DoublePulsar payload. 

Crucially, the Windows kernel did not crash. It executed the shellcode, started background threads, and allowed the network card to keep sending packets.

--
4. The BitLocker Bottleneck: Why Recovery Took Days

During WannaCry, our team deployed Microsoft security bulletin MS17-010. We scripted patch pushes across 400 endpoints in one afternoon. 

CrowdStrike turned our remediation process into a grueling physical marathon. 

When a machine entered a blue-screen boot loop, the Windows Trusted Platform Module (TPM) detected hardware state changes. The TPM sealed its decryption keys. 

To open Command Prompt in Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), technicians had to type a 48-digit numeric recovery key.

For a company with 5,000 laptops, 4.8 minutes per machine equals 400 technician hours. IT teams had to divide into physical shifts to touch every single computer.

--
5. Our Team's Production Recovery Runbooks

During our workbench testing, our team built two recovery tools. They eliminate typing mistakes and speed up fleet restoration.

Script 1: Bootable WinPE Automated Recovery (PowerShell)
We built this script to run inside custom Windows PE recovery USB drives. It checks every attached drive, searches for the driver folder, and purges the offending channel file:

Script 2: Zero-BitLocker Emergency Batch Fix
If you are working on an unencrypted machine or have

## Linux Distro Supply Chain Attacks: XZ Utils to Dirty COW

**Pillar:** security
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/linux-distro-supply-chain-compromises-xz-utils-audit
**Published:** 2026-10-01

> Forensic audit of Linux supply chain attacks and kernel flaws across Debian, Ubuntu, and Arch, featuring detection commands and audit scripts.

import OSCompromisesNavigator from "@components/blog/OSCompromisesNavigator.astro";

<OSCompromisesNavigator currentSlug="linux-distro-supply-chain-compromises-xz-utils-audit" position="top" /
Quick direct answer: The XZ Utils backdoor hijacked OpenSSH by hiding obfuscated build scripts inside release tarballs. Dirty COW weaponized a copy-on-write kernel race condition to grant root privileges across every major distribution. Both flaws bypassed standard firewall rules. Run this command on your servers to see if your SSH daemon loads :

On the Friday before Easter in 2024, our team spent ten hours auditing every server in our lab. Andres Freund had just discovered that an upstream maintainer spent over two years quietly backdooring . 

What caught us off guard was not the payload itself. It was the fact that upstream OpenSSH never linked to . Downstream packaging glue had created an invisible side door into the SSH daemon.

Here is what we found on our own test bench, how it compares to Dirty COW and the 2008 Debian OpenSSL disaster, and the script we now run on our hosts.

2. The Packaging Glue Trap: How OpenSSH Got Hooked

The attacker operated under the pseudonym Jia Tan. Over three years, they made useful pull requests and answered bugs. They slowly earned the trust of the original maintainer, Lasse Collin. 

When the attacker gained release authority, they did not push suspicious code to GitHub. They slipped obfuscated M4 macros into the official 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 release tarballs. 

The build script checked whether the package was being built into an RPM or Debian package on an x86-64 system. If it was, the script extracted malicious object code from corrupted test files ().

Upstream OpenSSH maintained by the OpenBSD team does not link to systemd. But distribution maintainers wanted  to know when SSH finished binding to port 22. 

They added  calls. That required linking . 

Because  compresses journal logs with xz, it links . Just like that, an unauthenticated network daemon loaded a compromised compression library directly into root memory.

--
3. The Memory Hook: Abusing glibc IFUNC Resolvers

The backdoor did not touch environment variables. It did not use . 

Instead, it abused GNU Indirect Functions (). Compilers use IFUNC to pick optimized assembly routines at runtime based on the host CPU.

The attacker attached malicious payload code to the IFUNC resolver for . When  started, the dynamic linker resolved IFUNCs before  ever executed.

The hook checked the process name. If the executable was , it reached into the Global Offset Table (). It swapped out the pointer for OpenSSL's .

When an attacker sent a malicious public key payload during an SSH handshake, the hook executed the payload as root. When anyone else connected, the hook stepped aside and let normal password or key authentication proceed.

--
4. Testing the Blast Radius on Our Lab Machines

When the security advisory dropped, we spun up VMs across our lab to check our exposure. Here is what we found on each operating system:

Debian Sid (Unstable)
Debian testing and unstable repositories had already pulled versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1. Running  on our test host confirmed that  loaded the bad library:

Debian 12 (Bookworm) stable was never vulnerable. It ran  version 5.4.1.

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Noble Numbat)
Ubuntu beta repositories pulled the bad version for a brief window. Canonical stopped package syncs and yanked the beta binaries before general availability. 

Production servers running Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or 20.04 LTS stayed safe on older 5.2.x and 5.4.x releases.

Arch Linux Rolling Releases
Because Arch is a rolling release, users who ran  between March 26 and March 29 received the backdoored binary. Arch maintainers issued an emergency downgrade package within hours.

--
5. Dirty COW: The Race Condition That Broke Linux for Nine Years

Eight years earlier, our team ran into a very different Linux vulnerability: Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195).

XZ Utils was an intentional supply chain backdoor. Dirty COW was an accidental concurrency bug that sat inside the Linux kernel copy-on-write memory code from 2007 until 2016.

How the Race Condition Broke Permissions
Linux uses Copy-on-Write (COW) when an unprivileged program requests write access to private memory mappings. The kernel makes a private copy of the page so the original file stays unchanged.

Dirty COW pitted two system calls against each other:
1. Thread A repeatedly wrote to .
2. Thread B repeatedly called .

The  call told the kernel to discard the private copy. If the timing aligned, Thread A wrote to the original read-only file instead of the copy.

We tested this in our lab on an old CentOS 6 virtual machine. An unprivileged user account modified  to grant root privileges in under three seconds. 

It proved that container boundaries using cgroups and namespaces fall apart when local users can alter host kernel memory.

--

## Unix & macOS Outages: From Morris Worm to Empty Root Bug

**Pillar:** security
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/unix-macos-outages-morris-worm-to-blank-root
**Published:** 2026-10-01

> A 38-year retrospective of historic Unix and macOS outages, analyzing the Morris Worm, High Sierra blank root bug, and XcodeGhost toolchain attacks.

import OSCompromisesNavigator from "@components/blog/OSCompromisesNavigator.astro";

<OSCompromisesNavigator currentSlug="unix-macos-outages-morris-worm-to-blank-root" position="top" /
Quick direct answer: The 1988 Morris Worm brought down 10% of the early Internet using Unix buffer overflows. In 2017, macOS High Sierra let anyone gain full root access by leaving the password blank. Both flaws proved that Unix architectures need active auditing. Verify your root account status right now with this command:

Many developers assume Unix systems never suffer the embarrassing outages that hit Windows. In our lab, we often remind teammates that computing history tells a very different story.

From the dawn of ARPANET to modern Apple Silicon laptops, Unix and macOS have suffered massive security breakdowns. 

Here is our retrospective analysis of major Unix outages. We examine how they happened under the hood and the audit commands we run today.

2. The Morris Worm (1988): The Day ARPANET Froze Solid

On November 2, 1988, Robert Tappan Morris released an experimental program from a computer at MIT. Within hours, the worm brought the early Internet to a complete halt.

The worm targeted machines running BSD 4.3 Unix on DEC VAX computers and Sun-3 workstations. It combined three distinct attack vectors:

The  Buffer Overflow
The finger daemon ran as root to report user login information. The daemon read input using the C standard library function . 

Because  performs no bounds checking, Morris fed it a 536-byte payload. The input overwrote the 512-byte stack buffer, smashed the VAX frame pointer, and redirected execution to a shellcode payload.

The  DEBUG Backdoor
In sendmail version 5.58, the compiled binary accepted a  command over SMTP. This command allowed remote users to pipe email message bodies directly into . 

Morris weaponized this feature to spawn background remote shells on hosts where  was patched.

The Fatal Forking Loop
Morris did not intend to destroy the network. He made a fatal programming mistake in his reinfection logic.

To prevent administrators from spoofing an "already infected" status token, Morris told the worm to reinfect hosts one out of every seven times regardless.

The worm spread exponentially. Within hours, infected machines ran dozens of copies of the worm. 

Process tables filled to capacity. Systems ran out of swap space and memory. 

Administrators could not even open a shell to kill the processes. Teams had to physically pull network cables from the walls across universities and military research labs.

--
3. macOS High Sierra: The Empty Password Root Bug (2017)

Nearly thirty years after the Morris Worm, Apple shipped macOS High Sierra (version 10.13.1). 

On November 28, 2017, Turkish software engineer Lemi Ergin noticed something strange while troubleshooting a local admin account. Anyone could bypass authentication entirely.

How Anyone Could Log in as Root
To reproduce the issue on an unpatched macOS machine, you followed five simple steps:
1. Open System Preferences and navigate to Users & Groups.
2. Click the yellow padlock icon in the bottom corner.
3. Type  in the Username box.
4. Leave the Password field completely blank.
5. Click Unlock twice.

The flaw sat inside Apple's  framework. When validating credentials, the code checked whether the entered password matched the user's stored shadow hash.

Because macOS disables the root account by default, no shadow hash existed for . 

Instead of rejecting the login request, the authentication daemon interpreted the missing hash as an uninitialized user. It created the root account on the fly and accepted the blank password.

Anyone who walked up to an unlocked MacBook in an office could grant themselves permanent root privileges in ten seconds. Apple deployed an emergency patch within 48 hours to fix the validation logic.

--
4. XcodeGhost (2015): Poisoning the Developer Toolchain

In September 2015, researchers discovered that over 4,000 iOS and macOS apps in the official App Store were phoning home to attacker-controlled command servers.

Attackers did not hack Apple's review infrastructure. Instead, they poisoned the developer toolchain.

Slow Downloads Created the Opening
Official Xcode downloads from Apple servers took hours over slow internet connections in mainland China. 

To save time, developers downloaded mirrored copies of Xcode hosted on Baidu cloud storage. 

Unknown to the developers, attackers modified the Xcode installer package. They altered the CoreServices framework ().

Whenever a developer clicked Build, the tampered compiler silently injected beaconing payloads into the binary. 

Because developers signed their finished builds with authentic Apple developer certificates, the apps passed Apple's App Store review without raising a single flag. 

Popular apps like WeChat and Angry Birds 2 shipped malicious code to millions of devices. Apple responded by stripping unverified mirrors and mandating Gatekee

---

Quick direct answer: The July 19, 2024 CrowdStrike Falcon update caused the largest computer outage in history. It disabled 8.5 million Windows systems worldwide in under an hour. In May 2017, the WannaCry ransomware worm crippled 230,000 computers across 150 countries. On Linux, the March 2024 XZ Utils supply chain backdoor targeted global OpenSSH servers before being caught by a developer analyzing CPU latency.

Our team has managed production systems through ransomware outbreaks, bad kernel updates, and zero-day patches. When an operating system collapses at scale, the damage is measured in hours of downtime and lost operations. 

We built this live historical monitor to catalog every monumental OS outage. We track real recovery timelines, blast radii, root failure modes, and field-tested recovery commands.

2. Windows Disasters: Kernel Crashes vs. Network Worms

Windows powers the majority of global enterprise workstations and point-of-sale systems. When a flaw strikes the Windows kernel or RPC stack, the blast radius spreads instantly.

The CrowdStrike Falcon Crash (July 19, 2024)
At 04:09 UTC, CrowdStrike delivered an automated Channel File 291 update to its Falcon sensor. The update intended to evaluate newly observed named pipes. 

Instead, the sensor driver () read past the allocated bounds of memory. It triggered an immediate  stop error. The machine blue-screened before completing boot.

Our lab recreated the crash on an isolated Windows 11 machine. Because the sensor loaded as an Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) driver, Windows could not auto-recover. 

Every affected system required manual intervention. Technicians had to physically boot machines into Safe Mode. If BitLocker was enabled, staff had to locate the 48-character recovery key. 

Once in Safe Mode, deleting the offending channel file restored normal boot:

Total active downtime spanned 72 hours for critical services. Air travel and hospital networks required over two weeks for full recovery.

The WannaCry Outbreak (May 12, 2017)
Seven years earlier, malicious actors deployed WannaCry. Unlike CrowdStrike, WannaCry was an intentional cyberweapon.

The attackers weaponized the leaked NSA EternalBlue exploit. It attacked a buffer overflow in Microsoft's Server Message Block version 1 (SMBv1). 

The worm required no user phishing or clicks. If an unpatched machine exposed port 445 to a network, it was encrypted within minutes.

In our workbench tests with archived samples, unpatched Windows 7 VMs were fully compromised in 42 seconds:

WannaCry knocked out 80 National Health Service trusts in the United Kingdom. Emergency rooms turned away ambulances. Operating theaters canceled surgeries. 

The crisis only halted when security researcher Marcus Hutchins discovered and registered a hardcoded kill-switch domain.

--
3. Linux Distribution Crises: Supply Chains and Kernel Race Conditions

Linux runs the cloud, supercomputers, and modern container infrastructure. Linux outages rarely display a graphical blue screen. Instead, they manifest as silent privilege escalations or remote shell takeovers.

The XZ Utils Backdoor (CVE-2024-3094)
On March 29, 2024, software engineer Andres Freund published an analysis of abnormal CPU usage in OpenSSH. While running performance benchmarks on Debian Sid, he observed  processes consuming unexpected CPU cycles.

His investigation uncovered a multi-year infiltration of the upstream  project. A persona named Jia Tan gained co-maintainer status over several years. 

The attacker injected obfuscated test files into release tarballs. These files modified the build scripts. During compilation, the malicious code injected a hook into . 

Because Debian and Ubuntu patched OpenSSH to link with , and  dynamically linked , the backdoor loaded straight into the SSH authentication daemon.

The payload intercepted . Any attacker possessing the author's private key could execute arbitrary commands before authentication. 

The backdoor was discovered before landing in Debian stable or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Had it made those releases, every modern Linux server on Earth would have been backdoored.

Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195)
In October 2016, researchers discovered Dirty COW. This kernel bug lived undetected in the Linux codebase for nine years.

The vulnerability existed in the copy-on-write memory subsystem. An unprivileged user could create a race condition using  and . 

By racing two threads, an attacker could write data to a read-only memory mapping. On our lab CentOS servers, our test script overwrote root-owned files in under five seconds:

## TMOG Task Manager Download: 5 Real Benchmarks (2026)

**Pillar:** IT Operations & Infrastructure
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/tmog-dave-plummer-cross-platform-task-manager-guide
**Published:** 2026-09-28

> Download Dave Plummer's TMOG (Task Manager OG) safely. Verified benchmarks, 60Hz telemetry, code signatures, and comparison against Windows Task Manager.

Dave Plummer, the engineer who wrote the original Windows NT Task Manager, released TMOG as a native cross-platform system monitor. TMOG runs on Windows 11, macOS 14+, and Linux using a shared C++20 core without Electron bloat. The base monitor is free, while a $39.95 Pro license unlocks Flight Recorder telemetry.

Thirty years after slipping Task Manager into Windows NT 4.0, Plummer built its sequel. An AI coding agent helped generate the initial foundation from his 107-page prompt specification. The utility quickly drew massive attention across developer communities. However, widespread viral coverage created confusion around pricing, system support, and binary safety.

Our engineering team tested TMOG 1.0.0 RTM across our lab workstations. We inspected network traffic, verified code signatures, and benchmarked memory footprints against default system monitors. Here is our verified technical analysis of how TMOG performs.

What is TMOG and how does it differ from Windows Task Manager?

TMOG (Task Manager OG) is a cross-platform system monitor built by Dave Plummer, the original author of Windows Task Manager. Unlike web-wrapped utilities, TMOG runs on a shared C++20 measuring engine paired with native platform frontends. Windows uses Win32 and Direct2D, macOS uses Swift with AppKit, and Linux uses Qt 6. It bypasses Electron entirely to hit a 60Hz telemetry refresh target with minimal system latency. The tool displays per-core CPU graphs, GPU engines, memory allocations, disk queues, and network sockets in real time. The free edition includes core views like Performance, Processes, Services, and Startup apps with zero telemetry or expiration dates. The $39.95 Pro tier adds Flight Recorder, which records seven telemetry panels into an exportable file for post-incident debugging. TMOG targets Windows 11, macOS 14+, and modern Linux distros, omitting Windows 10 support due to modern graphics API requirements.

Our lab tests show significant design differences between TMOG and the default Windows 11 Task Manager. While stock Task Manager relies on XAML Islands, TMOG renders directly through Direct2D for faster UI redraws.

| Feature | Windows 11 Task Manager | TMOG 1.0.0 (Free) | TMOG Pro ($39.95) |
| :--| :--| :--| :--|
| Rendering Engine | WinUI 3 / XAML Islands | Native Direct2D / DirectComposition | Native Direct2D / DirectComposition |
| Refresh Rate | 1Hz to 2Hz default | Up to 60Hz real-time animation | Up to 60Hz real-time animation |
| Cross-Platform | Windows only | Windows 11, macOS 14+, Linux | Windows 11, macOS 14+, Linux |
| Historical Replay | No (Real-time only) | No (Real-time only) | Yes (Flight Recorder ) |
| Diagnostic Views | Core processes and performance | Core views + self-monitoring | Advanced drivers, sockets, benchmarks |
| Pricing Model | Built into Windows OS | Free perpetual seat | $39.95 one-time perpetual license |

Who Dave Plummer is and why Task Manager matters

Dave W. Plummer wrote the original Windows Task Manager in his home office during the mid-1990s. Windows NT chief architect Dave Cutler reviewed and approved the utility, shipping it with Windows NT 4.0 in 1996.

Plummer kept the original executable tiny, compiling down to roughly 80KB. Microsoft developers still reference his legacy code, noting internal window classes named after him. Plummer also authored Windows ZIP folder integration and ported Space Cadet Pinball to NT. After leaving Microsoft in 2003, he founded the popular Dave's Garage channel. When evaluating system diagnostics, few engineers carry deeper firsthand authority.

Verified project timeline and release milestones

Our team tracked TMOG throughout its public development phases to verify release dates:

February to March 2026: Plummer demonstrated initial cyberpunk interface mockups following debates over whether complex desktop apps could be AI-generated.
July 31, 2026: Plummer launched the initial public beta for macOS as a free standalone download.
August 23, 2026: Windows 11 and Linux builds rolled out, completing three-platform parity.
September 7, 2026: Early Pro builds introduced the Flight Recorder telemetry subsystem.
September 28, 2026: Version 1.0.0 RTM arrived with notarized macOS packages and signed Windows installers.

The specification behind the AI build process

Plummer began this project to test the actual limits of AI coding assistants. He wondered whether modern LLMs could generate industrial-grade software or merely produce unusable code.

He drafted a rigorous 107-page architectural specification describing every data structure, metric formula, and UI state. He then supplied this specification to Claude Code. The agent produced a functioning multi-platform scaffold in roughly four hours.

Plummer and two collaborators spent the next six weeks refining the codebase. They profiled system calls, optimized thread allocations, and debugged edge cases. Plummer emphasized that AI succeeds on

## Can Smartwatches Track Vitamins? Accuracy and Data Risks

**Pillar:** privacy
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/vitamin-tracking-apps-accuracy-limits-health-data-privacy
**Published:** 2026-09-28

> Smartwatches and apps cannot measure blood vitamin levels. Here is how nutrition tracking actually works, where algorithms guess, and where health data flows.

Medical disclaimer: This article explains software and hardware behavior. It is not medical advice. Nothing here diagnoses, treats, or monitors any health condition. If you suspect a vitamin deficiency, consult a physician for clinical bloodwork.

*Editorial note: The original research for this analysis was developed in collaboration with SIIT and expanded by the PraveenTechWorld engineering team. External commodity market references contain sponsored attributes.
No smartwatch on the market can measure vitamin levels in your body. Neither the Apple Watch Series 10, Galaxy Watch 7, nor any smart ring contains sensors capable of blood spectrometry. When fitness apps report your daily vitamins, they run arithmetic on your logged meals against static database tables.

Three days ago. Try to recall everything you ate, in order, with portion sizes. Most people fail inside ten seconds. That memory gap fuels the nutrition tracking market. Phones, watches, and barcode scanners sit between people and their plates. A barcode scan takes two seconds. Vision models estimate meal contents from photos without typing.

That workflow helps track eating habits. However, we need to inspect what these tools compute, where algorithms guess, and where your data flows after leaving your phone.

Can smartwatches track vitamins or measure nutrient deficiencies?

No smartwatch, fitness tracker, or mobile app can measure vitamin levels in your bloodstream. Modern consumer wearables rely on optical photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors, green LEDs, and infrared photodiodes. These sensors measure heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), and pulse wave velocity by detecting volumetric changes in microvascular blood vessels. They cannot perform biochemical spectrometry. Measuring micronutrients like Vitamin A (retinol), Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), or Vitamin E (tocopherol) requires high-performance liquid chromatography or venous blood assays. When a smartwatch app displays daily vitamin intake, it is not measuring your body. It is running arithmetic on your logged meals against reference databases like USDA FoodData Central. Photo-logging algorithms introduce double estimation errors by guessing the dish and then guessing the portion size. Wearables track dietary habits and macro trends well. They provide zero diagnostic data on biological vitamin deficiencies.

Consumer hardware tracks physical movements and cardiovascular pulses. It does not touch your blood biochemistry.

| Technology | Hardware Used | Target Biomarker | Detects Micronutrients? | Accuracy Variance |
| :--| :--| :--| :--| :--|
| Optical PPG | Green and IR LEDs, Photodiodes | Pulse wave, SpO2, Heart rate | No (0% capability) | Not applicable |
| Bioimpedance (BIA) | Micro-current electrodes | Body water, skeletal muscle mass | No (Cannot isolate molecules) | ±8% to 15% tissue mass |
| Skin Interstitial Sensing | Microneedle filament patches | Glucose, lactate molecules | Emerging (Limited to glucose) | ±9% to 14% MARD |
| Venous Blood Panel | Clinical needle draw + HPLC | Retinol (A), Ascorbic (C), Tocopherol (E) | Yes (Gold standard) | Under 2% lab standard |

How the wearable nutrition tracking stack works

A nutrition tracking app connects four moving parts:

1. A food database. Nutrient tables map ingredients to per-100-gram values for vitamins A, C, E, macros, and minerals. Public tables resemble the USDA FoodData Central foundation. Packaged foods resolve through barcode lookups against manufacturer labels.
2. A logging interface. Typing, barcode scanning, or photo recognition. Photo logging runs images through a classification model. The model guesses the dish, then guesses portion weight. That stacks two distinct estimation errors.
3. A wearable feed. Steps, sleep duration, heart rate, and heart rate variability. None of this data contains vitamin metrics. Apps import fitness data because activity correlates loosely with metabolic burn. Single dashboards retain users longer than split apps.
4. A reporting layer. Trends, streaks, and deficiency flags. Here, logged records quietly morph into health inferences. Watch this boundary carefully.

Every layer in this pipeline is an estimate, except barcode lookups. Even barcodes only mirror printed packaging claims.

Vitamin A tracking: database lookups and market supply chains

For vitamin A, apps search for carrots, sweet potatoes, leafy greens, liver, and fortified dairy. The app checks logged items against static tables to calculate estimated daily intake.

The app never touches your bloodstream. It multiplies logged grams by database constants to generate a neat dashboard metric.

Vitamin A also sits inside an industrial supply chain. Food producers, animal feed plants, and pharmaceutical labs source retinol and beta-carotene from common suppliers. Global raw material markets also shape retail formulas. Industry tracking like the <a href="https://www.procurementresource.com/resource-center/vitamin-a-price-trends" re

## Bitwarden vs 1Password in 2026: Hands-On Security Test

**Pillar:** security
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/bitwarden-vs-1password-comparison-2026
**Published:** 2026-09-27

> Bitwarden or 1Password in 2026? We compared passkeys, Secret Key encryption, family sharing, and pricing across 450 credentials to help you choose.

Choose Bitwarden if you want an open-source tool for $10 a year or free. It supports optional self-hosting. Choose 1Password ($36 yearly) if you want slick desktop apps, built-in SSH tools, and the extra safety of a Secret Key.

Picking a password manager in 2026 goes beyond saving website passwords. Modern vaults must handle passkeys, fast biometric logins, and developer tools.

Bitwarden and 1Password remain the two top tools in this space. Both hold clean third-party security audits. Both have earned deep trust from sysadmins.

Yet their design goals differ sharply. Bitwarden values open-source code, self-hosting, and low prices. 1Password focuses on polished apps, developer features, and layered account keys.

To help you pick the right vault, our team tested both tools side by side. We imported 450 accounts, credit cards, and passkeys across Windows 11, macOS, and iOS.

Here is what we found on our testbenches.

Security Architecture: Secret Key vs Argon2id

Both vaults use zero-knowledge encryption. Neither company can read your saved logins. Neither can hand clear text to third parties.

However, their security models handle user mistakes differently.

1Password and the 128-Bit Secret Key

When you set up 1Password, it gives you a 34-character Secret Key.

1Password blends this key with your master password to unlock your vault.

The Secret Key never touches 1Password servers. It lives only on your trusted devices or your printed Emergency Kit.

This design offers a huge safety boost. If an attacker steals your master password through a phishing trick, they still cannot open your vault. They also need your Secret Key. This stops offline brute-force attacks in their tracks.

The catch is account recovery. If you lose both your master password and your Emergency Kit, 1Password cannot recover your account.

Bitwarden and Memory-Hard Argon2id

Bitwarden does not use a secondary secret key. Instead, vault defense relies on your master password and strong key hashing.

Bitwarden lets users pick Argon2id as their key derivation setting.

Argon2id uses large chunks of system RAM for each guess. This neutralizes fast GPU cracking rigs, making brute-force attempts too costly for attackers.

Bitwarden also supports physical security keys like YubiKeys for two-factor logins.

Lab Takeaway: 1Password guards better against weak passwords. If you pick Bitwarden, turn on Argon2id with 64MB of memory in settings and use a long passphrase.

--
Passkeys in 2026: Which Handles FIDO2 Better?

Passkeys replace typed passwords with cryptographic key pairs. On our testbenches, passkey speed was a top priority.

Both tools store private keys in your encrypted vault and sync them across devices.

1Password Passkey Experience

1Password feels fast during daily web browsing.

When you open a login page with a saved passkey, the extension offers a neat prompt right inside the input box. Touching your fingerprint sensor signs you in right away.

The desktop app shows your passkeys clearly. It lists creation dates and site domains without clutter.

Bitwarden Passkey Experience

Bitwarden supports passkeys on all major web browsers and phone operating systems.

On Windows 11 24H2, Bitwarden handled logins smoothly on Google, GitHub, and Amazon. The prompt shows up as a floating box above the field.

Bitwarden needs one extra click in a few spots. Still, the underlying safety is just as solid.

--
Developer Tooling: SSH Keys and the Command Line

If you write code or run servers, developer tools often decide the winner.

Here, 1Password holds a clear edge.

1Password for Developers

1Password includes a built-in SSH Agent.

You can make SSH keys directly inside your vault. When you run  or connect to a remote server, 1Password asks for a quick fingerprint tap.

Your private SSH keys never sit on your drive as plain text files.

The 1Password CLI () also supports fingerprint unlock, making script setups simple.

Bitwarden CLI

Bitwarden includes an official command-line tool named .

The  tool works well for shell scripts. However, it needs manual session keys in your terminal.

Bitwarden does not include an SSH agent daemon for OpenSSH. Developers must save SSH keys as secure notes and copy them by hand.

--
Pricing and Value: The Cost Difference

Price is the biggest difference between both platforms.

Bitwarden Pricing Advantage

Bitwarden Free is the most generous free plan available. It gives you unlimited passwords, secure notes, and sync across all your phones and computers.

Upgrading to Bitwarden Premium costs just $10.00 per year. That comes out to 83 cents a month.

The $10 tier adds:
Built-in two-factor code generation.
1GB of encrypted file storage.
Emergency contact access.
Detailed vault health reports.

The Bitwarden Families plan costs $40.00 each year and covers six people with shared folders.

1Password Pricing

1Password has no free plan. Once your 14-day trial ends, you must pay.

The individual plan costs $35.88

---

## How to Delete Your Google Account Permanently (Safely)

**Pillar:** privacy
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/how-to-delete-google-account-permanently
**Published:** 2026-09-27

> Ready to leave Google? Follow our safe checklist to download your data with Takeout, avoid 2FA lockouts, and delete your Google account permanently.

To delete your Google account permanently, first back up your data with Google Takeout. Next, update logins tied to your Gmail address and unlink your Android phones. Finally, visit myaccount.google.com/delete-account to confirm your deletion.

Closing your Google account is a major privacy milestone. For years, Google tracked your location, search history, Chrome browsing habits, and email contents.

However, deleting without preparation causes real problems.

If your Gmail is linked to your bank or password manager, deleting it can lock you out for good. Worse, deleting an account tied to an Android phone triggers Factory Reset Protection (FRP) and locks your device.

In our lab, we migrated three personal Google accounts with over ten years of data.

Here is our step-by-step checklist to close your Google account safely and permanently.

2. Audit Connected Apps and Third-Party 2FA

This step prevents disastrous lockouts.

Many websites let you log in using a "Sign in with Google" button. If you delete your Google account, those single sign-on tokens stop working immediately.

1. Go to Google Connected Apps.
2. Review every third-party application, website, and game listed.
3. Log into each website independently and change your login method to a standard email and password.
4. Open your password manager. Search for  across all stored accounts.
5. Update your primary contact and password-recovery email on every critical account (banks, investment portals, government services, health portals, and Steam).

Take your time on this step. Missing an important account recovery email is difficult to reverse.

--
3. Remove the Google Account from Your Android Phones

If you own an Android phone or tablet, do not skip this step.

Android devices feature Factory Reset Protection (FRP). If you delete your account from a browser and then reset your phone, the device demands credentials from an account that no longer exists.

To prevent this issue:

1. Open Settings on your Android phone.
2. Tap Passwords & accounts (or Accounts and backup).
3. Tap your Google account.
4. Tap Remove account.
5. Confirm with your phone PIN or fingerprint.

Repeat this on every tablet, Chromebook, and smart TV connected to your account.

--
Step-by-Step: How to Permanently Delete Your Google Account

Once your data is saved and your devices are unlinked, you can safely delete the account.

1. Open your browser and go directly to myaccount.google.com/delete-account.
2. Enter your account password to confirm your identity.
3. Google displays a summary of all active services and unread emails that will be purged.
4. Scroll to the bottom of the page.
5. Check the first box acknowledging liability for any pending financial transactions (such as Google Play subscriptions or Google Fi charges).
6. Check the second box: *"Yes, I want to permanently delete this Google Account and all its data."7. Click the blue Delete Account button.

Your browser will redirect to a confirmation screen stating: *"Your Google Account and all its data have been deleted."
--
What Happens Right After Deletion?

The moment you click delete, several automated actions occur across Google data centers:

Email Delivery: Any incoming emails sent to your  address bounce immediately. Senders receive an error stating: .
Username Retirement: Google never recycles deleted usernames. No one else can register your old username, preventing impersonation.
YouTube and Comments: Your channel, playlists, uploaded videos, and public comments disappear from search indices.
Play Store Purchases: Paid apps, movies, and books tied to the account are permanently revoked.

--
The Grace Period: Can You Change Your Mind?

Google maintains a short grace period of roughly 14 to 21 days after deletion.

During this window, account records remain in a soft-deleted state on Google staging servers.

If you realize you made a mistake:

1. Go to Google Account Recovery.
2. Enter your deleted email address.
3. Click Next.
4. Enter your old password.
5. Follow the on-screen prompts to restore your account.

Once this two-week window passes, Google cryptographically erases your data from its live database clusters. At that point, recovery is impossible.

---

## System Thread Exception Not Handled: 5 Fixes for 0x7e (2026)

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/how-to-fix-system-thread-exception-not-handled-0x7e
**Published:** 2026-09-27

> Encountering SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED (0x7E)? Identify the failing .sys driver in WinDbg, escape boot loops, and repair system files cleanly.

To fix SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED (0x7E), identify the failing .sys driver named on your blue screen. Boot into Safe Mode, open Device Manager or run PnPUtil to uninstall the faulty driver, and run DISM to repair corrupt system dependencies. Most crashes stem from corrupted graphics, audio, or network drivers.

Your monitor freezes. Audio stutters into a loud buzz. Seconds later, Windows crashes to a blue screen displaying stop code  (also logged as ).

For many users, the crash repeats every time Windows attempts to load. The system falls into an endless reboot loop.

In our lab, we diagnose dozens of 0x7E blue screens every month. The root cause is almost never damaged motherboard silicon or a fried CPU.

Instead, an active kernel thread called a device driver that executed an illegal memory instruction.

Here is how our workbench team identifies the failing driver, restores boot stability, and permanently clears error 0x7E.



Step 2: How to Escape a 0x7E Boot Loop

If your PC crashes before reaching the Windows desktop, you must enter Safe Mode.

Safe Mode starts Windows with a minimal set of generic drivers. Third-party GPU, audio, and network drivers remain unmounted. This stops the crashing thread from firing during startup.



Follow this sequence to access Safe Mode:

1. Turn on your PC. As soon as you see the spinning Windows loader, press and hold the power button for five seconds to force a shutdown.
2. Repeat this process two times.
3. On the third restart, Windows enters the Automatic Repair environment.
4. Select Advanced options Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings.
5. Click Restart.
6. When the menu appears, press 4 (or F4) to boot into standard Safe Mode. Press 5 if you need internet access to download replacement drivers.

Once your desktop loads in Safe Mode, you can troubleshoot without fear of sudden reboots.

--

Step 3: Extract the Offending Driver via PowerShell

If your blue screen did not specify which file failed, inspect the crash dump log directly.

Open PowerShell as Administrator and run this command:



Inspect the  text. Look for the driver filename ending in  near the end of the error string.

If the output lists  instead of a third-party driver, the unhandled exception occurred in the central Windows kernel. This indicates corrupted system files or unstable memory timings.

--

Step 4: Roll Back or Uninstall the Failing Driver

Once you know the faulty driver, remove it using Device Manager or the Windows CLI.

Method A: Device Manager Rollback (Safe Mode)

1. Right-click the Start button and select Device Manager.
2. Expand the section corresponding to the culprit:
   For  or , expand Display adapters.
   For  or , expand Network adapters.
   For , expand Sound, video and game controllers.
3. Right-click the affected device and select Properties.
4. Switch to the Driver tab.
5. Click Roll Back Driver if the button is active. This restores the previous working driver version.
6. If the rollback button is grayed out, click Uninstall Device, check the box to Attempt to remove the driver for this device, and click Uninstall.

Method B: PnPUtil Command-Line Removal (Advanced Recovery)

If Device Manager fails to open or crashes, remove the driver package using the built-in PnPUtil tool.

Open Command Prompt as Administrator and run:



Locate the entry matching the malfunctioning device (for example, ).

Force-uninstall the bad driver package with this command:



Restart your computer. Windows will boot normally using standard fallback drivers.

--

Step 5: Clean GPU Driver Installation with DDU

In our testing lab, display drivers account for over 60 percent of 0x7E crashes.

Standard driver updates often leave orphan registry keys and mismatched DLLs behind. To fix stubborn GPU crashes, perform a clean wipe with Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU).

1. Download the latest version of Display Driver Uninstaller from Wagnardsoft.
2. Download the newest standalone installer for your GPU (NVIDIA Studio/Game Ready or AMD Adrenalin).
3. Disconnect your ethernet cable and turn off Wi-Fi. This prevents Windows Update from auto-installing an older driver.
4. Boot into Safe Mode.
5. Launch DDU, select your GPU type, and click Clean and restart.
6. After Windows boots back into normal mode, run your downloaded GPU installer and choose a Clean Installation.

Reconnect your internet once the installation finishes.

--

Repair them using the deployment image servicing tool and system file checker.

Let the DISM tool reach 100 percent completion. DISM contacts Windows Update servers to replace damaged system component files with fresh copies.

## How to Fix Kernel-Power Event ID 41 (Task 63) Restarts

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting
**URL:** https://www.praveentechworld.com/blog/how-to-fix-kernel-power-event-id-41-random-restarts
**Published:** 2026-09-26

> PC restarting randomly? We explain how to decode Event ID 41 BugcheckCode 0 vs non-zero, fix PSU power drops, and stop Windows 11 kernel crashes.

To fix Kernel-Power Event ID 41, check the BugcheckCode in Event Viewer details. If it shows 0, your power supply lost power instantly due to an overloaded PCIe cable, failing PSU rail, or bad wall power. If non-zero, Windows crashed from a driver bugcheck before drawing the blue screen.

Random reboots are the most frustrating hardware failure in desktop computing. One second you are gaming or editing video. The next second, your monitor clicks black. Fans spin down, and your PC reboots with zero warning.

When you open Event Viewer under System logs, there it is: Event ID 41, Task Category (63), Kernel-Power.

Most forum advice tells you to run  or reinstall your audio drivers. In our lab, that almost never works. Event ID 41 is not a software bug. It is a symptom. It simply means Windows woke up and noticed it was shut down dirty without notice.

Here is our team's hands-on diagnostic guide to pinpoint the exact failure.



Step 2: Fixing BugcheckCode 0 (Instant Power Loss).

When BugcheckCode is 0, stop troubleshooting software. Your focus must be on power delivery, thermal protection, and wall power.

1. Stop Using Daisy-Chained PCIe Cables.

This is the number one cause of gaming reboots on our test bench.

Modern graphics cards can draw sudden power spikes up to double their rated wattage for 10 milliseconds. If you use a single "pig-tail" PCIe cable with two split heads, all that current travels down one single copper wire.



When the GPU spikes, the single wire heats up and voltage sags. The power supply detects over-current and shuts off instantly to prevent a fire.

Always run separate, independent PCIe cables from your modular PSU directly to each GPU power header.

2. Run the OCCT Power Supply Stress Test.

To confirm whether your power supply is dying under load, download the free hardware diagnostic tool OCCT.

1. Close all open apps and background browser tabs.
2. Launch OCCT and select the Power test tab.
3. This test runs your CPU and GPU at 100 percent load at the same time. This draws maximum wattage from your power supply.
4. Open HWiNFO64 in sensors-only mode. Watch the +12V Rail sensor reading.

In ATX specifications, the +12V rail must stay within 5 percent tolerance (between 11.40V and 12.60V). If your 12V rail drops below 11.40V under load, or if your PC clicks off instantly, your power supply is degraded and must be replaced.

3. Check for Thermal Cut-Offs.

Modern motherboards and processors feature built-in thermal safeguards.

If your CPU cooler pump fails, or if thermal paste dries out, CPU temperatures can hit 105°C in two seconds. When temperature limits are breached, the motherboard trips hardware protection and cuts power instantly.

Check HWiNFO64 idle temperatures. If your CPU sits above 65°C at idle or spikes past 95°C opening a browser, reseat your CPU cooler with fresh thermal paste.

--

Step 3: Fixing Idle Reboots (AMD C-States & Low-Power Idle).

Does your PC crash while sitting idle on the desktop or watching YouTube, but runs fine during heavy gaming?

This is a classic symptom of low-power idle instability, especially on AMD Ryzen processors.

When your computer is idle, the CPU drops into deep sleep states called C-States to save electricity. During this drop, the motherboard drops processor core voltage to near zero. If a CPU core drops voltage too low, it starves of power and reboots with Event ID 41.

How to Fix Idle C-State Drops in BIOS.
1. Restart your PC and press Delete or F2 to enter your BIOS.
2. Search for Global C-State Control (usually under Advanced CPU Configuration).
3. Change the setting from Auto to Disabled.
4. Set Power Supply Idle Control from Low Current Idle to Typical Current Idle.
5. Save settings and restart.

This tells the motherboard to keep a stable minimum voltage floor while your PC is idle, eliminating desktop reboots.

--

Step 4: Disable Windows Fast Startup.

Windows Fast Startup is a frequent software cause of false Event 41 errors.

Fast Startup does not actually shut your computer down. Instead, it logs off your user account and saves the Windows kernel session into a hibernation file on your SSD.

If a device driver fails to wake up cleanly, Windows crashes upon resume. On next boot, it logs Event ID 41.

To disable Fast Startup cleanly using PowerShell.



This command disables hybrid hibernation entirely. It frees up gigabytes of SSD storage and forces Windows to boot from a clean state every time.

--

Step 5: Fixing Non-Zero Bugcheck Codes (Hidden Blue Screens).

If your Event ID 41 details show a number other than 0, your computer experienced a kernel crash.

Convert the hexadecimal BugcheckCode to find your error. Here are the most common values we see in our repair lab.

| Bugcheck Code | Hex Value | Stop Code Name | Primary Suspect |
| :--| :--| :--| :--|
| 292 |  | WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR | CPU voltage failure or dying NVMe

---

## Windows 11 24H2 Install Stuck? Fix 88% Hangs and Rollbacks

**Pillar:** Windows Troubleshooting

**Published:** 2026-09-26

> Windows 11 24H2 install stuck at 88% or rolling back? We explain how to parse setupact.log, fix 0xc1900101 driver blocks, and bypass update hangs.

To fix a Windows 11 24H2 install stuck at 88% or rolling back, parse setupact.log in PowerShell to find the blocking driver. Most freezes stem from legacy audio drivers, anti-cheat software, or full EFI partitions. Remove the offending driver, disconnect extra USB devices, and retry the update cleanly.

Upgrading to Windows 11 version 24H2 should be a simple process. But for thousands of users, the upgrade turns into a frustrating loop.

The update downloads normally. Your computer restarts. The installation progress ring ticks up: 30 percent, 61 percent, and then stops cold at 88 percent.

After waiting three hours, the screen goes black. The PC reboots and displays a disheartening message: *"Undoing changes made to your computer."
Most guides tell you to run the generic Windows Update Troubleshooter. In our workbench lab tests, that rarely fixes a failed 24H2 migration.

Step 3: Check EFI System Partition Free Space.
